top_categories.workout_context: 8,432ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
At mile 60 of 94, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
90ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Boone Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
At Boone Gran Fondo, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
Boone Gran Fondo's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 94 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 94 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Boone Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
8,432ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Boone Gran Fondo, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
The aerobic base that lets you ride mixed terrain at tempo for 94 miles without cracking. No shortcuts.
Low-cadence force work for 8,432ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.heat: August in Boone, North Carolina, USA can bring heat. If the forecast warrants it, include controlled heat exposure before Boone Gran Fondo and rehearse the drinking and electrolyte plan you tolerate in training. Do not introduce a fixed sodium protocol solely from this preview.
race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Boone Gran Fondo’s 94 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Boone Gran Fondo with 8,432ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%.
race_overlay.terrain: Mixed terrain at Boone Gran Fondo requires surface adaptability. Include weekly rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Durability, and TT Threshold to prepare you for 94 miles of mixed terrain in Boone, North Carolina, USA.
